details:
MEDICUS AI — AUTONOMOUS CREW HEALTH AND CLINICAL DECISION-SUPPORT CONSOLE

Medicus AI is an onboard medical intelligence and clinical decision-support console designed to protect astronaut health during space missions when real-time communication with Earth flight surgeons is delayed or unavailable.

  1. WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS

Medicus AI unifies live spacesuit telemetry, a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) medical copilot, and deep-learning diagnostic imaging into a single onboard web console:

  • Continuous Suit and Wearable Telemetry Monitoring: The console tracks live physiological and environmental metrics, including heart rate (bpm), blood oxygen (%), core body temperature (°C), and suit CO2 levels (%). When an abnormality occurs, such as a sustained 18% heart rate elevation alongside rising suit CO2 for 12 minutes, the agent flags early CO2 buildup, prioritizes recovery actions, and displays a 4-step emergency protocol: securing tethers, switching to the backup scrubber, alerting crew and ground control, and returning inside if CO2 stays above 1%.
  • Dual-Interface RAG Copilot and AI Assistant: Crew members can interact via a floating Medicus Copilot button or expand into the full AI Assistant panel using text, photos, or video attachments. On the Flask backend (/api/chat), incoming queries are embedded with text-embedding-3-small, matched against a FAISS vector index (multi_pdf_faiss_index.bin), combined with session conversation history, and answered using Groq (llama-3.1-8b-instant).
  • Onboard Disease-Specific Diagnosis Models: The dashboard monitors key spaceflight health indicators, including bone density loss, heart rhythm (HRV), Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS), lung health, and daily radiation dose. It also integrates a brain MRI classifier (/predict) powered by a TensorFlow/Keras InceptionV3 model (299 x 299 input size) that classifies MRI scans into glioma, meningioma, pituitary, or no tumor.
  • Radiology Overlays and Health Reports: Diagnostic scans display visual AI overlays with confidence scores, such as a distal radius hairline fracture at 92% confidence. An integrated AI reporting pipeline (gpt-4o-mini) generates structured clinical summaries covering condition descriptions, causes, symptoms, treatment steps, and prevention for sharing with flight surgeons.
  1. BENEFITS OF THE PROJECT
  • Autonomous Triage During Communication Delays: Space missions experience signal delays (such as a 12-minute Earth link delay) and offline periods. Running diagnostics and clinical retrieval on board eliminates wait times during emergencies.
  • Lower Cognitive Load Under Stress: Translates multi-sensor trends into clear, numbered action steps so astronauts can execute emergency procedures quickly.
  • Transparent, Explainable Reasoning: Instead of giving unverified conclusions, the AI Assistant lists the visual and biometric evidence behind its findings, such as correlating a flat forearm rash along a sleeve liner edge with normal wearable temperature data to identify mild contact irritation.
  • Immediate Emergency Access: Removing login and signup gates from the copilot backend allows crew members to access medical guidance without credential bottlenecks during critical events.
  1. INTENDED IMPACT
  • Enabling Deep-Space Human Exploration: As missions extend farther from Earth, crews require autonomous medical decision support. Medicus AI bridges the gap between raw suit vital monitoring and having a flight surgeon on board.
  • Remote Healthcare Applications on Earth: Beyond spaceflight, this offline-capable console architecture can assist medics and health workers in remote clinics, polar stations, ships, and disaster-relief zones where specialist doctors and continuous internet access are unavailable.
  1. TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES, HARDWARE, AND SOFTWARE USED
  • Frontend Technologies: HTML5, CSS3 (responsive CSS Grid layout, adaptive light and dark themes, ARIA accessibility roles, and reduced-motion support), and JavaScript (FormData requests and sessionStorage state management).
  • Backend and Web Framework: Python, Flask, and Flask-CORS.
  • Deep Learning and Computer Vision: TensorFlow, Keras (InceptionV3 model mri_Inceptionv3_f2x64.h5), and NumPy for image preprocessing.
  • RAG and Vector Search: FAISS vector index (multi_pdf_faiss_index.bin) paired with JSON document stores (multi_pdf_documents.json) and session chat persistence.
  • Large Language Models and Embeddings: OpenAI text-embedding-3-small for vector embeddings, OpenAI gpt-4o-mini for diagnostic report generation, Groq llama-3.1-8b-instant for fast RAG responses, and Groq llama-3.3-70b-versatile for automatic session title generation.
  • Target Hardware and Sensor Architecture: Designed for spacecraft console displays, crew tablets, and live telemetry streams from spacesuits and wearable health monitors.
  1. HOW OUR PROJECT IS CREATIVE
  • Seamless Copilot-to-Assistant Continuity: Medicus AI pairs a floating Ask Copilot widget (with quick clinical prompt chips) with a full-screen AI Assistant panel. Both interfaces share the same RAG session ID, allowing a crew member to start a quick check mid-task and continue in the full assistant workspace without losing context.
  • Spaceflight-Specific Clinical Design: Every vital sign, emergency protocol, and diagnostic model is tailored to aerospace medicine, including suit CO2 scrubber failure, microgravity dehydration, bone density loss, SANS optic disc changes, and radiation exposure.
  • Unified Clinical Workspace: Bringing live telemetry alerts, RAG medical lookup, and deep-learning radiology into a single interface reduces context switching during high-stress medical events.
  1. KEY FACTORS OUR TEAM CONSIDERED
  • Communication Latency and Offline Resilience: We built the console around onboard inference and asynchronous report sharing so critical triage does not depend on a live Earth connection.
  • Human-in-the-Loop Safety: Medicus AI is explicitly positioned as a decision-support tool rather than a replacement for a flight surgeon. Every diagnostic result includes confidence bars, visual overlays, and itemized reasoning for verification.
  • Ergonomics and Emergency Usability: Under acute stress, fine motor control and reading speed drop. We used color-coded status tags (Normal, Watch, Critical), clear typography, keyboard-accessible controls, and single-tap emergency actions.
  • Modular Architecture: Separating the RAG chat endpoint (/api/chat) and diagnostic imaging endpoint (/predict) inside a unified Flask backend allows additional disease-specific models to be added without redesigning the user interface.
